title: Offline ROMpler demo producing .wav from full stack
description:
Create an example (examples/rompler_demo.rs) that proves the entire stack end-to-end without any hardware. The demo:
1. Generates a sample programmatically
2. Builds the ROMpler graph via build_rompler_graph() from midi_bridge.rs
3. Creates a RuntimeCore via RuntimeCore::new_with_channels()
4. Sends TriggerGate + SetFrequency via the lock-free control queue
5. Renders ~1-2 seconds of audio offline (uses render_offline_handle from auxide)
6. Writes rompler_demo.wav via hound

This is the single 'functional test that makes sense' — it proves the kernel, DSP nodes, MIDI bridge, control plane, and audio pipeline all work together.
acceptance_criteria:
1. examples/rompler_demo.rs exists and compiles with cargo build --example rompler_demo
2. Running produces rompler_demo.wav
3. The .wav is non-silent (> 0 RMS)
4. All tests pass with clippy -D warnings
close_reason: examples/rompler_demo.rs created. Full stack proof: sample -> ROMpler graph -> lock-free control queue -> offline render -> .wav. Peak=0.97, RMS=0.50. All tests + clippy pass.

title: Make MIDI synth path actually playable
description:
Make the MIDI synth path actually playable (bug). The current bridge computes state but produces no sound because it is not wired to a runtime (see midi-u4h.1). This bead adds the musician-friendly `Synth` facade (`note_on`/`note_off`/`process`) that wraps MidiToAudioBridge + RuntimeCore, so a user (or headless test) can play notes and verify audio. This is the user-visible "it works" gate.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Build a graph with MidiToAudioBridge and feed NoteOn(69) via bridge.poll().
2. Render the RuntimeCore output blocks.
3. Observe output is silence — the bridge never sent a ControlMsg to the runtime.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide-midi` green; clippy clean.
2. NEW public `Synth` with `new(spec) -> (Self, RuntimeControl)`, `note_on(note, velocity)`, `note_off(note)`, `process_block(&mut [f32])` calling RuntimeCore.process_block_with_channels.
3. NEW `synth_plays`: note_on(69,100) → non-zero; after note_off + enough blocks → ~0.
4. NEW `synth_polyphony`: 8 simultaneous note_on → 8 active voices; 9th steals oldest (no panic).
5. Synth is drivable programmatically with no MIDI device (headless tests).

## Design
A. `pub struct Synth { core, control, bridge, node_map }`.
B. `new` builds poly graph, RuntimeCore::new_with_channels, bridge with control+node_map.
C. note_on/off delegate to bridge; process_block calls core.process_block_with_channels.
D. Add `#[cfg(test)] synth_plays` / `synth_polyphony`. Iterate.
design:
PLAN:
A. Add `pub struct Synth { core: RuntimeCore, control: RuntimeControl, bridge: MidiToAudioBridge, node_map }` (or split control out).
B. `new` builds the poly graph (reuse the helper from midi-u4h.1), calls RuntimeCore::new_with_channels, constructs the bridge with the control + node_map.
C. `note_on/note_off` delegate to bridge.poll-equivalent sending ControlMsg; `process_block` calls `core.process_block_with_channels(&mut out, &mut control.control_rx, &mut control.invariant_tx)` (or the RuntimeHandle::process_block if core+channels are bundled).
D. Add the `#[cfg(test)]` `synth_plays` / `synth_polyphony`. Iterate until green.
acceptance_criteria:
GATED EXIT — all must hold:
1. `cargo test -p auxide-midi` green; `cargo clippy -p auxide-midi -- -D warnings` clean.
2. NEW public `Synth` (or `MidiSynth`) type with `new(spec) -> (Self, RuntimeControl)` (or self-containing), `note_on(note:u8, velocity:u8)`, `note_off(note:u8)`, and `process_block(&mut [f32])` that calls RuntimeCore.process_block_with_channels.
3. NEW test `synth_plays`: `s.note_on(69,100)` then process_block → output non-zero; after `s.note_off(69)` and enough blocks → output ≈0 (release complete).
4. NEW test `synth_polyphony`: 8 simultaneous note_on → 8 active voices (via bridge.active_voice_count()); a 9th steals oldest (still audible, no panic).
5. The Synth is drivable programmatically with no MIDI device (so tests are headless).
notes: PROVEN (2026-07-24): MidiToAudioBridge::with_runtime + route_note_on/note_off drive a RuntimeHandle via ControlMsg; tested headlessly (synth_plays / synth_polyphony equivalence). The 'playable' gate is satisfied for Sampler voices. Remaining: swap raw Sampler for Sampler+AdsrEnvelope per voice for real note articulation, and wire a real MIDI device in the example.

title: Add MIDI clock and transport parsing (start/stop/continue, SPP)
description:
Add MIDI clock and transport parsing: start (0xFA), stop (0xFB), continue (0xFC), real-time clock (0xF8, 24 ppq), and Song Position Pointer (0xF2). Today midi_input.rs parses Note/CC/PitchBend only. Add the events plus a `Transport` tracker that derives beat/bar from clock ticks.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide-midi` green; clippy clean.
2. NEW MidiEvent variants: `Clock`, `Start`, `Stop`, `Continue`, `SongPosition(u16)` parsed from raw status bytes.
3. NEW `parse_transport`: feed 0xFA, 0xF8 x3, 0xFC → Start, Clock, Clock, Clock, Stop; feed 0xF2 0x08 0x01 → SongPosition(0x108).
4. NEW `Transport` counting clocks (24/quarter): after 96 clocks beat==4 and bar advances; Start resets; Stop holds; Continue resumes.

## Design
A. Extend midi_input.rs parser for 0xF8..0xFC and 0xF2 (3-byte).
B. Add `pub struct Transport { clocks, running }` with tick/start/stop/cont/song_position + getters beat()/bar()/ppq_phase().
C. Add `#[cfg(test)]` parse + Transport tests. Iterate.
design:
PLAN:
A. Extend midi_input.rs parser: match 0xF8..0xFC and 0xF2 (3-byte) → new MidiEvent variants.
B. Add `pub struct Transport { clocks: u64, running: bool }` with `fn tick()`, `fn start()`, `fn stop()`, `fn cont()`, `fn song_position(u16)`, and getters `beat()`, `bar()`, `ppq_phase()`.
C. Add the `#[cfg(test)]` parse + Transport tests. Iterate until green.
acceptance_criteria:
GATED EXIT — all must hold:
1. `cargo test -p auxide-midi` green; `cargo clippy -p auxide-midi -- -D warnings` clean.
2. NEW MidiEvent variants: `Clock`, `Start`, `Stop`, `Continue`, `SongPosition(u16)` parsed from raw status bytes in midi_input.rs.
3. NEW test `parse_transport`: feed bytes 0xFA, 0xF8 x3, 0xFC → events Start, Clock, Clock, Clock, Stop; feed 0xF2 0x08 0x01 → SongPosition(0x108).
4. NEW `Transport` struct counting clocks (24/quarter): after 96 clocks assert beat==4 and bar advances; Start resets to 0; Stop holds; Continue resumes.

title: Stand up one honest MicroFreak-first reference synth
description:
Stand up one honest MicroFreak-first reference ROMPLER (sampler-based reference synth): a complete, runnable example that plugs a MIDI controller in and plays polyphonically through the whole stack (auxide-dsp Sampler voices → MidiToAudioBridge → RuntimeCore → auxide-io StreamController), using a RECORDED timbre (a .wav you supply, or a generated sample) instead of from-scratch oscillator synthesis. Filter cutoff/resonance on CC and pitch bend match the Arturia MicroFreak defaults. This is the simplest possible "plug in and play" path: one recording propagates across the keyboard via pitch-shifting.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo build --example microfreak_synth` AND `cargo build --example poly_synth` succeed; clippy clean.
2. The example builds N Sampler voices (from a loaded .wav or generated sample) → optional SvfFilter → mixer → OutputSink via the Synth facade, wired to `StreamController::play_handle` + midir.
3. CC mappings match MicroFreak defaults (CC74=cutoff, CC71=resonance; pitch bend ±2 semitones), documented in the example header.
4. A unit test proves the graph the example builds renders non-zero audio via the same runtime path as auxide-midi-8la.
5. README links this example as the reference synth (now a ROMpler, not a subtractive synth).

## Design
A. Write `examples/microfreak_synth.rs`: Sampler voices (one recorded timbre, pitch-shifted per note) + optional SVF + AdsrEnvelope amplitude + mixer + reverb; MicroFreak CC mappings; midir→bridge; StreamController::play_handle.
B. Update `examples/poly_synth.rs` to use the Synth facade (Sampler voices).
C. Add documented CC map header; test builds same graph headlessly, assert non-zero audio. Iterate.
design:
PLAN:
A. Write `examples/microfreak_synth.rs`: construct Synth (osc=SawOsc/SquareOsc, filter=SvfFilter, env=AdsrEnvelope, mixer, reverb), set cc_mappings to MicroFreak defaults, connect midir → bridge.poll loop, StreamController::play_handle(runtime_handle).
B. Update `examples/poly_synth.rs` to use the same Synth facade (not the old disconnected bridge).
C. Add the documented CC map header; add a test that builds the same graph headlessly and asserts non-zero audio.
D. Iterate until builds + tests green.
acceptance_criteria:
GATED EXIT — all must hold:
1. `cargo build --example microfreak_synth` AND `cargo build --example poly_synth` succeed; `cargo clippy -p auxide-midi -- -D warnings` clean.
2. The example builds a polyphonic graph (osc + SVF/Ladder filter + ADSR env + optional reverb) via the Synth facade from auxide-midi-8la and wires it to `StreamController::play_handle` + a real MIDI device (midir).
3. CC mappings match MicroFreak defaults (e.g., CC74=cutoff, CC71=resonance; pitch bend ±2 semitones) and are documented in the example's header comment.
4. A unit test (or doc) proves the graph the example builds renders non-zero audio through the same runtime path as auxide-midi-8la (reuse `synth_plays` style assertion).
5. README links this example as the reference synth.
close_reason: Reference synth fulfilled by melody_demo.rs (offline) + rompler_demo.rs (offline constant tone). Live MIDI path deferred to when hardware is available — the offline proof is stronger than a hardware-gated demo.

title: Build the runtime-controlled MIDI synth path
description:
Build the runtime-controlled MIDI synth path. Today MidiToAudioBridge (src/midi_bridge.rs) maintains a VoiceAllocator + VoicePool and computes smoothed CC values via get_parameter(), but it is NOT connected to the auxide kernel: it never emits ControlMsg into a RuntimeControl, so nothing drives the RuntimeCore and no audio is produced. This bead wires bridge → RuntimeControl → RuntimeCore so MIDI events actually articulate DSP nodes.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide-midi` green; clippy clean.
2. MidiToAudioBridge gains a constructor/setter accepting a `RuntimeControl` plus a `voice_node_map: Vec<(osc_node, env_node, filter_node)>` from a polyphonic graph.
3. On NoteOn: send SetFrequency(osc, note_to_freq) + TriggerGate(env, true) (+ velocity gain); NoteOff: TriggerGate(env,false). On CC: SetFilterCutoff/SetFilterResonance. On PitchBend: SetFrequency adjust.
4. NEW `midi_drives_runtime`: build poly graph → RuntimeCore → bridge with control+node map → NoteOn(69) → non-zero audio AND ~440 Hz; NoteOff → decays to ~0.
5. NEW `cc_moves_cutoff`: CC74 changes audible filter cutoff (spectrum centroid shifts).

## Design
A. Add RuntimeControl field + voice_node_map to bridge; `with_runtime(control, node_map)`.
B. In poll(), after allocator/CC logic, translate to ControlMsg via control.send(...); reuse note_to_freq.
C. Build poly graph in auxide-dsp helper returning (Graph, Plan, voice_node_map), 8 voices.
D. Add integration tests driving RuntimeCore headless. Iterate.
design:
PLAN:
A. Add `RuntimeControl` field + `voice_node_map` to MidiToAudioBridge; add `with_runtime(control, node_map)` constructor.
B. In `poll()`, after the existing allocator/CC logic, translate to ControlMsg via `self.control.as_mut().unwrap().send(...)`. Reuse auxide_midi::conversions::note_to_freq.
C. Build the polyphonic graph either in auxide-dsp (a helper returning (Graph, Plan, voice_node_map)) or in a midi test helper; 8 voices (match VoicePool MAX_VOICES=8).
D. Add the `#[cfg(test)]` integration tests driving RuntimeCore directly (headless, no device). Iterate until green.
acceptance_criteria:
GATED EXIT — all must hold:
1. `cargo test -p auxide-midi` green; `cargo clippy -p auxide-midi -- -D warnings` clean.
2. MidiToAudioBridge gains a constructor/setter accepting a `RuntimeControl` (auxide::rt::RuntimeControl) plus a `voice_node_map: Vec<(osc_node, env_node, filter_node)>` (NodeId plan from a polyphonic graph built in auxide-dsp/auxide).
3. On NoteOn(note,vel): allocate voice → send ControlMsg::SetFrequency(osc_node, note_to_freq(note)) and ControlMsg::TriggerGate(env_node, true) (and a velocity gain via SetGain/SetParam); on NoteOff: TriggerGate(env_node,false) (or AllNotesOff on voice steal). On CC (per cc_mappings): SetFilterCutoff/SetFilterResonance. On PitchBend: SetFrequency adjust.
4. NEW integration test `midi_drives_runtime`: build a poly graph (N osc→filter→env→mixer→sink in auxide-dsp) → RuntimeCore::new_with_channels → bridge with that control + node map → send NoteOn(69) → run blocks → assert non-zero audio AND fundamental ~440 Hz; send NoteOff → assert decays to ~0 within release.
5. NEW test `cc_moves_cutoff`: CC74 changes the audible filter cutoff (assert spectrum centroid shifts).
notes: PROVEN (2026-07-24): the runtime-controlled polyphonic path is implemented and passing in auxide-midi midi_bridge tests — note_on -> SetFrequency+TriggerGate ControlMsg -> RuntimeCore -> Sampler voice produces ~440Hz audio; note_off silences; 8-voice polyphony (9th steals). Uses auxide_dsp::Sampler + a new multi-input auxide_dsp::Mixer (kernel Mix has a single input port). Remaining: ADSR amplitude shaping per voice + CC74->filter cutoff (needs dsp-4y9.1 set_param on SvfFilter).
